text:
Watch 'Morning Jolt' Stock Markets Around the World Are Soaring Again Japanese, Hong Kong and European markets continue Wednesday's Wall Street rally, while China, Taiwan and Korea take a break for the Lunar New Year. Oil prices are also in positive territory as are the U.S. futures indices. But the dollar is still showing weakness. By Jonathan Braude Feb15,20186:55AMEST 
The Japanese markets saw the main action in Asia this morning as China, Korea were closed for the Lunar New Year holiday while Hong Kong closed early, up a strong 1.97% at 3115.43. 
The Nikkei rallied for the first time in four days - despite the continued strength of the yen, which normally has a negative effect on the export-oriented index. The dollar spot index fell 0.3%, with the yen climbing 0.6% against the greenback, to ¥106.40. The euro was up 0.3% at $1.246. 
The Nikkei was up 1.47% at 2,146.98, while the Topix was up 0.97% at 1,719.27. 
In Australia the S&P/ASX200 index closed up 1.16% at 5,908.99. 
In pre-market trading 
In Europe, the FTSE100 was up 0.58% at 7,255.82, the DAX was up 0.80% at 12,437.76 and in Paris the CAC40 rose 1.46% to 5,240.79. 
That followed the better mood last night on Wall Street. U.S. markets closed in positive territory Wednesday for the fourth straight session, with the S&P 500 shaking off a negative start to close 1.34% up at 2,698.63 and the DJIA closed at 24,893.49 or 1.03% up. Traders shrugged off the earlier jitters over rising consumer prices. 
On the futures market the Dow Jones mini was up 244.0, or 0.98% at 25,107.00 with an implied opening price of $240.51 
In pre-market trading this morning Apple ( AAPL ) was up over 1.3% on the back of Berkshire Hathaway's ( BRK.A ) ( BRK.B ) 's statement in a regulatory filing last night that it has boosted its Apple stake by 23% since the end of September. The Warren Buffet-led investor also said it has taken a new stake in Teva Pharmaceutical Industries ( TEVA ) - a factor which pushed up Teva's New York listed ADR by almost 7% to $20.67. 
Cisco Systems ( CSCO ) jumped 7.46% to $45.23 in the pre-market after last night's announcement that it raised its share buyback program by $25 billion and plans to bring back $67 billion of funds held over seas to take advantage of changed U.S. tax laws. 
Oil prices were mixed, after yesterday's lower than expected crude inventory data. WTI Crude was up 0.21% at $60.73. While Brent Crude was down 0.28% at $64.18. 
In Zurich Nestle ( NSRGF ) NSRGY dropped over 2.6% after full year results showed organic growth came in below expectations at 2.4%. The company said it expected improved growth in 2018 and the results were anyway mixed. While reported sales were below consensus, underlying operating margin of 16.4% was had of the consensus of 16.2%. 
But the Nespresso owner also opened the way to the sale of its 23% stake in French cosmetics group L'Oreal. It said it won't renew its partnership with L'Oreal's founding Bettencourt family when it expires late next month and won't increase the stake. Activist Dan Loeb has been pushing the Swiss food company to sell the holding. If you liked this article you might like
